EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The single most critical development of the past 24 hours centers on the stalled US-Iran negotiations, mediated by Pakistan, as Iran refuses to transfer highly enriched uranium and asserts its right to levy transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz. This impasse, coupled with US intelligence reports indicating Iran's faster-than-anticipated military reconstruction during the current ceasefire, significantly elevates the risk of renewed escalation and destabilization across the Middle East. US President Trump has warned of "very drastic" action if an agreement is not reached.

IRAN
Negotiations between Iran and the United States are ongoing, with Pakistan acting as a mediator. An Iranian official indicated that while no deal has been reached, gaps have narrowed. US Secretary of State Rubio confirmed "some progress" and "good signs" but cautioned that the Iranian system appears "split and fragmented." The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman dismissed media speculations on nuclear details, stating that negotiations primarily focus on ending the war across all fronts, including Lebanon. However, major points of contention remain Iran's uranium enrichment program and control over the Strait of Hormuz. US President Trump reiterated that "one way or another, they won't have nuclear weapons," and the conflict will end "very soon." Arab officials reportedly expect the war to resume after the Hajj period.

Reports conflict regarding Iran's highly enriched uranium. Some sources claim Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued a directive that 60% enriched uranium must remain within Iran, a position an unnamed senior Iranian official affirmed to Al Jazeera as consistent and stating "no new order has been issued," with Iran capable of reducing enrichment itself. Conversely, the White House denied Reuters' report on Khamenei's order as "incorrect." President Trump declared the US will "get the uranium, we don't want it and will probably destroy it," emphasizing Iran will not be permitted to possess it.

Iran reasserted its intent to manage and potentially levy transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz, with reports suggesting discussions with Oman for a permanent transit fee system, including exemptions for allies like Russia and China. US President Trump and Secretary of State Rubio explicitly rejected this, with Rubio stating it would render a diplomatic agreement impossible. US CENTCOM reported that its forces enforced a blockade on Iranian ports, disabling 4 ships and redirecting 94 commercial vessels. The IRGC Navy, however, announced that 31 vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours under its coordination and security.

US intelligence, as reported by CNN, indicates that Iran is rebuilding its military capabilities, including drone production and missile sites, "much faster than initially estimated" during the ongoing 6-week ceasefire. Estimates suggest Iran could fully restore its drone attack capability within six months. The IRGC Navy's political deputy emphasized the readiness of Iranian Armed Forces to counter any aggression. Trump claimed 85% destruction in Iran. The Intelligence Organization of Iran's IRGC stated that US intelligence assesses "time is not on our side" and that Iran's initiatives and threats must be taken seriously.

Internally, nightly nationwide rallies were held in Kerman, Ardabil, and Tehran's Enghelab and Sadeqiyeh Squares to demonstrate support for the Islamic Republic, show solidarity with the Armed Forces, and pledge allegiance to the "new Leader." Two individuals, Ramin Zale and Karim Maroofpour, were executed for "forming a group to disrupt state security" and "membership in a terrorist organization." President Pezeshkian pledged the government's full support to strengthening the Armed Forces. The Vice Chairman of the Cultural Committee of the Parliament, Ali Yazdikhah, stated that global internet access restrictions would continue due to "security considerations."

ISRAEL
Israeli forces from the 'The Hammer' Brigade (14) eliminated a terrorist in northern Gaza who crossed the "yellow line" and posed an immediate threat. Additionally, a Hamas Nukhba terrorist was neutralized in central Gaza earlier this week. In the West Bank, forces from Battalion 932 and Reserve Battalion 5016 arrested three Hamas-affiliated terrorists in Hebron who were planning an immediate shooting attack. Another individual promoting terror activities was apprehended in Deir al-Ousoun. IDF and Border Police successfully thwarted an attempt to smuggle 26 pistols at the eastern border.

The Israeli home front experienced alerts for hostile aircraft intrusion in Kiryat Shmona, Manara, and Misgav Am. All these incidents were subsequently declared false alarms or contact was lost with the suspicious aerial target. The Rearmament Chief of Staff, Major General Eyal Zamir, affirmed that the IDF remains on high alert and continues operations in all sectors during the Shavuot holiday. The IDF warned against entering designated closed military areas in Southern Israel during Shavuot due to ongoing training.

The Israeli military faces a manpower shortage, requiring up to 17,000 new recruits. The IDF announced the establishment of a new 'Alumot' unit, a technological-operational center focused on developing AI capabilities and information processing platforms for field forces.

Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu reportedly pushed for an immediate resumption of offensive operations against Iran, but US President Trump refused, demanding more time and citing a need to "save lives." Ambassador to the US, Yechiel Leiter, publicly condemned remarks made by Minister May Golan regarding MK Rabbi Gilad Kariv. The head of Trump's Gaza Peace Council, Nikoli Mladenov, sharply condemned Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's actions. The Wall Street Journal detailed Israel's AI-based manhunt, employing facial recognition and AI analysis of vast digital data to identify and target all Hamas and Islamic Jihad operatives involved in the October 7 attacks.

Civilians in the north continue to be affected, with the Rosh Hanikra tourism site reporting two employees remain hospitalized, one fighting for their life, following a Hezbollah drone attack a week prior.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, a drone strike in Beit Lahia resulted in one fatality and two injuries. IDF forces eliminated one terrorist in northern Gaza and another Hamas Nukhba terrorist in central Gaza. Aftermath footage showed an Israeli drone strike targeting a tent in the Al-Mawasi area of southern Gaza.

The humanitarian situation in Gaza remains dire, with the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA) reporting over 125,000 cases of infections linked to rats and parasites during the first five months of the current year.

Regarding future arrangements, Nikoli Mladenov, head of Trump's Gaza Peace Council, proposed a "roadmap" for Gaza's future, encompassing Hamas demilitarization, increased humanitarian aid, establishment of a technocrat council, formation of a new Palestinian police force, deployment of an international stabilization force, and eventual Israeli withdrawal from Gaza.

Settler activity continues in the West Bank, with CCTV footage capturing Israeli settlers stealing a Palestinian shepherd's flock in Masafer Yatta. Israeli occupation forces raided Bani Na'im, east of al-Khalil, detaining Palestinian residents. Near the Tapuach Junction in Samaria, a suspected ramming attempt occurred with no injuries, and the driver was apprehended in Hawara village.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched a drone attack that reportedly targeted an Iron Dome launcher in the occupied town of Shomera. Other reports indicate Hezbollah drones attacked Kiryat Shmona and its surroundings. Footage circulated showing Hezbollah targeting an Israeli military vehicle in Bayyada, southern Lebanon, with a drone on May 17.

In response, Lebanese media reported Israeli attacks in several southern villages. Aftermath footage displayed Israeli airstrikes targeting Tebnine and Mansouri in southern Lebanon. A burial ceremony was held for children reportedly killed in Israeli airstrikes on Deir Qanoun AlNahr.

The Lebanese Ministry of Health updated casualties since March 2 to 3,089 killed and 9,397 injured. The condition of Commander of Armored Brigade 401, Colonel Meir Biderman, and combat photographer Sergeant Sh., who were severely wounded by an explosive drone in southern Lebanon, has reportedly improved, and both are now stable and conscious. A tourism site in Rosh Hanikra reported that two of its workers remain hospitalized, with one in critical condition, following a Hezbollah drone attack a week ago.

Economically, the Lebanese Finance Minister informed Reuters that the country's economy is projected to shrink by 7-10% this year due to the ongoing conflict.

Politically, Hezbollah condemned US sanctions against its supporters as an "intimidation attempt." The US Department of State sanctioned nine individuals for supporting Hezbollah and undermining Lebanon's stability, including Lebanese parliament members, an Iranian diplomat, and Lebanese security officials, also offering a $10 million reward for information disrupting Hezbollah's financial mechanisms. The US Treasury also sanctioned Mohammad Reza Raoof Sheibani, Iran's Ambassador to Lebanon. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam met with former ambassador Simon Karam to discuss future negotiation rounds. Israeli officers were quoted questioning the efficacy of remaining in Lebanon given the lack of achievements and inability to use full force.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Multiple explosions were reported in Erbil, northern Iraq, including an alleged assassination attempt on Khurshid Harki and a drone strike targeting the headquarters of Iranian Kurdish opposition parties in the Soran district. Baghdad Operations Command conducted a controlled detonation of war remnants near Baghdad International Airport.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi stated his opposition to the use of Iraqi territory or airspace for aggression against neighboring countries. Yemen's Ansarullah movement leader Abdul-Malik Al-Houthi claimed that US companies are plundering Iraqi oil and that the Israeli enemy is not an invincible force.

The Iraqi General Company for Ports declared an emergency after losing contact with two Bolivian-flagged ships, Bridge 1 and Bridge 2, which had not entered Iraqi waters, and no distress signals were received. The wife and brother of Karo Khosravani were reportedly kidnapped in Sulaymaniyah, northern Iraq.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's Al-Hadath network reported that Supreme Leader Khamenei's final decision is not to transfer enriched uranium to Washington. Cristiano Ronaldo scored two goals, leading Al-Nassr to win the Saudi League championship. The Financial Times reported that Saudi Arabia has halted new consulting contracts and delayed payments due to budget deficits and the consequences of the Iran war, as part of its Vision 2030 cost-cutting measures.

Anwar Gargash, a senior adviser to the UAE government, stated that Iran's "bullying and threatening behavior" has eroded trust among Gulf states, dismissing Iran's claim of controlling the Strait of Hormuz as an "unachievable fantasy." Israeli media reported the UAE is purchasing loudspeakers from Israel for use in air raid sirens.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Kuwait has been "isolated by the Iran war," with its daily 2 million barrels of oil exports halted due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Consequently, essential imports now arrive via Saudi land routes at six times the cost of sea transport. The Al Khalifa government in Bahrain reportedly ordered the detention of over 40 prominent Shiite scholars and clerics for 60 days and froze their bank accounts. The IRGC has reportedly threatened to seize Bahrain and convert it into a military base if hostilities resume.

Qatar's Foreign Minister, Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, engaged in a phone call with Egyptian Foreign Minister Bader Abdelatty to discuss regional developments and de-escalation efforts. The UK announced a $5 billion trade deal with the GCC countries, projected to add $3.7 billion annually to the British economy and remove 93% of tariffs on British goods, aiming to send a message of stability.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Stalled Iran-US Negotiations:** Mediation efforts by Pakistan are ongoing, but a significant impasse remains over Iran's highly enriched uranium and its potential control over the Strait of Hormuz. US Secretary of State Rubio noted "some progress" but also a "fragmented" Iranian system. Trump has warned of "very drastic" action if an agreement is not reached.
2.  **Iran's Uranium Stance:** Conflicting reports emerged regarding Iran's highly enriched uranium. Some sources claim Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered it to remain in Iran, while the White House denied this report as "incorrect." Trump insists the US will take and destroy it.
3.  **Strait of Hormuz Dispute Intensifies:** Iran reasserted its intent to manage and potentially levy transit fees in the Strait, a move explicitly rejected by President Trump and Secretary of State Rubio, who called it an "impossible" condition for diplomacy. US CENTCOM reported disabling 4 ships and redirecting 94 commercial vessels enforcing a blockade, while the IRGC Navy reported 31 successful transits.
4.  **Rapid Iranian Military Reconstruction:** CNN, citing US intelligence, reported Iran is rebuilding its military capabilities, including drone production and missile sites, "much faster than initially estimated" during the current 6-week ceasefire, with potential for full drone attack capability restoration within 6 months.
5.  **US Military Depletion:** The Washington Post, citing Pentagon assessments, revealed the US military significantly depleted its advanced missile interceptor stockpiles (200+ THAAD, 100+ SM-3/SM-6) defending Israel from Iranian attacks, exceeding Israel's own usage.
6.  **Israeli Operations in Gaza & West Bank:** IDF eliminated one terrorist in northern Gaza and a Hamas Nukhba terrorist in central Gaza. In Hebron, three Hamas-affiliated terrorists planning a shooting attack were arrested, along with another terror operative in Deir al-Ousoun.
7.  **Lebanese Casualties & Economic Impact:** The Lebanese Ministry of Health reported 3,089 killed and 9,397 injured since March 2. The Lebanese Finance Minister estimated a 7-10% economic contraction due to the war. The condition of the Commander of Armored Brigade 401 and a combat photographer, severely wounded by a drone, improved to stable and conscious.
8.  **International Condemnation of Israeli Actions:** Italy's Foreign Minister formally requested EU sanctions against Israeli Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir for his treatment of "Global Sumud Flotilla" activists. The UK, Australia, and Poland also summoned Israeli ambassadors, and Spain deported 44 activists via Turkey.
9.  **Gulf States' Economic Pressure:** Saudi Arabia halted new consulting contracts and delayed payments due to budget deficits and the Iran war. Kuwait's daily 2 million barrels of oil exports have reportedly ceased due to the Strait of Hormuz closure, with essential imports now costing six times more via land routes, leading to its isolation.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are high. The fundamental disagreements over Iran's enriched uranium and control of the Strait of Hormuz, coupled with President Trump's warnings of "very drastic" actions and Israel's reported push for immediate renewed attacks, indicate a strong potential for the current ceasefire to break down. Iran's reported rapid military reconstruction further suggests preparation for continued conflict. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's intent to impose transit fees directly clashes with US opposition and CENTCOM's enforcement. The Northern Israel/Southern Lebanon border remains a critical flashpoint due to ongoing Hezbollah drone attacks and Israeli retaliatory strikes. Iran's nuclear program, particularly the enriched uranium, constitutes a clear red line for the US and Israel, increasing the risk of military action targeting facilities. The US military's depletion of advanced missile interceptors raises questions about the long-term sustainability of its current air defense posture. Iran's rapid reconstruction efforts suggest an increased offensive and defensive posture.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is complex, with President Trump confirming negotiations with Iran and stating that Iran will not achieve nuclear weapons. He also indicated the US would take and destroy Iran's enriched uranium and opposes Strait of Hormuz fees. However, internal US administration divisions are reported, with Trump reportedly favoring continued negotiations over military pressure, despite arguments from Secretary of State Rubio and War Secretary Pete Hegseth. Trump refused Netanyahu's call for immediate renewed attacks on Iran, citing a need for more time. The US sanctioned nine individuals for supporting Hezbollah and undermined Lebanon's stability, including an Iranian diplomat and Lebanese officials, and offered a $10M reward for information disrupting Hezbollah's financial mechanisms. The US also sanctioned Iran's Ambassador to Lebanon. The US deployed 5,000 additional troops to Poland.

Among Gulf States, Oman is reportedly discussing a permanent transit fee system for the Strait of Hormuz with Iran. Qatar and Egyptian foreign ministers discussed regional de-escalation. Saudi Arabia and Qatar reportedly prefer to avoid renewed conflict, while the UAE and Israel reportedly advocate "tough policies" against Iran. The UAE senior adviser criticized Iran's "bullying and threatening behavior." The GCC signed a $5 billion trade deal with the UK for stability.

In Europe, Italy's Foreign Minister formally requested EU sanctions against Israeli Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir for mistreating "Global Sumud Flotilla" activists. France rejected NATO involvement in the Strait of Hormuz, citing the alliance's North Atlantic remit. The European Parliament passed an anti-Iranian resolution, calling for increased political pressure and sanctions. The European Commission predicted the Iran war would stifle growth and drive up inflation in the Eurozone.

Russia's President Putin discussed with Chinese President Xi the idea of transferring and storing Iran's enriched uranium in Russia. Russia's Ministry of Defense released footage of nuclear forces exercises, with Putin declaring the nuclear triad a reliable guarantor of sovereignty and nuclear weapons use as a "last resort." China, in turn, threatened retaliation against planned EU trade restrictions.

Pakistan continues to actively mediate between Iran and the US. There are conflicting reports on whether Pakistani Chief of Army Staff Asim Munir will arrive in Tehran tonight. Poland and Australia summoned Israeli ambassadors over the treatment of flotilla activists, with Poland advising its citizens against travel to Israel. Spain announced the deportation of 44 Spanish activists from Israel via Turkey. The UK also summoned the Israeli ambassador for similar reasons.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions exist regarding the status of Iran negotiations, with reports alternating between "gaps narrowed" and "contacts exploded." US Secretary of State Rubio's remarks on "some progress" and "good signs" are juxtaposed with his acknowledgement of Iran's system being "split and fragmented," raising questions about the coherence and reliability of the Iranian negotiating position.

A significant point of contention is the alleged order by Mojtaba Khamenei for highly enriched uranium to remain in Iran. This claim by Reuters was explicitly denied as "incorrect" by the White House, and an Iranian official stated no such new order was issued, with Iran capable of reducing enrichment independently. This discrepancy could stem from internal power struggles within Iran, intentional disinformation, or differing intelligence assessments.

The Washington Post's report on the depletion of US advanced missile interceptors used to defend Israel highlights potential long-term strategic vulnerabilities for the US and raises questions about burden-sharing among allies.

Propaganda indicators are evident across multiple sources. Iranian state media consistently frames events through a nationalistic and anti-Western lens, emphasizing "patriotism," "strategic upper hand," and "battlefield superiority." President Trump's rhetoric, including claims of "85% destruction in Iran" and "total control of Strait of Hormuz," appears aimed at projecting strength. The White House's X post depicting a "killed" Ali Khamenei is a clear example of psychological operations or deliberate misinformation. Commentators like 'omid dana' contribute opinion-based predictions and internal political criticisms that are largely unverified. The use of "imported citizens from Africa" in Iranian "patriotism" videos suggests an effort to manufacture a narrative of diverse internal support.

Reporting gaps include the precise details of the latest US proposal to Iran and the full extent of Iran's response. Specifics on US intelligence assessments regarding Iran's military reconstruction are generalized. There is also limited detailed information on Israeli military operations beyond specific targets or incidents. The "Beit Shemesh Explosion" is mentioned by Press TV as an event Israel is allegedly concealing, but no further details are provided by any source. The situation regarding the two "missing ships" in Iraqi waters remains unexplained.
